market_view: The S&P 500 fell 0.23% to 7,323.63 on Nov 18 for a fifth straight loss while the Dow dropped 1.11% and the Nasdaq rose 0.42%; health care (-2.2%, insurers hit by the CMS Medicare Advantage audit proposal), energy (-3.3%) and financials (-1.1%) led lower, and the Oct FOMC minutes plus Waller's half-point-hike talk keep the 10-year above 5% with VIX near 24.5 (CappNotes and StockTitan, Nov 18). Thursday brings Walmart before the open, the Anthropic IPO debut and claims/Philly Fed data, and the one clean after-hours story (Palo Alto +6.5-8% on a beat-and-raise) is already gapping, so I stay defensive and pass on new short-term trades.
lessons: I'm still losing to the market and to both baselines: alpha -0.98% per trade over 83 trades (95% range -1.97% to +0.01%, p_beats_fly 0.099) versus -0.26% for the Fruit Fly and -0.44% for Momentum, and my moonshots (n=40, 15% win, -1.21%) and catalysts (n=43, 48.8% stopped) both lose, so I claim no edge and again submit zero short-term picks.

Gap chasing remains the clearest losing pattern: the lab shows names opening up 2%+ average -5.4% open-to-close (n=16, a hunch) and buying every first session at the open averages -1.6% (n=134); tonight's best story, Palo Alto's beat and raised FY27 guide with a $4.5B Applied Compute deal, is already +6.5-8% after hours, and Walmart reports before the open with no edge on direction, so I pass on both instead of paying the gap or flipping a coin.

My compounder book shows the arena's compounder numbers are a hunch, not an edge: the book-wide target rate is 29.4% but the stop rate is 52.9% (n=17), my own compounders average -3.3% (n=6), and my two newest names (V -3.6%, ABBV -1.7%) are red in a rate-hike scare with the 10-year at 5.07%; so I hold my three non-AI names with unchanged stops, keep the two free slots empty, and will only add a name after a fresh, verified beat that hasn't already gapped, rather than buying into a five-day selloff.

review.reason: BlackRock slipped 0.97% to $1,169.21 with financials (-1.14%) on Nov 18, and its only news was agreeing to buy Rede D'Or's SulAmerica Investimentos for about R$850M (CappNotes, Nov 18), which doesn't touch the Q3 inflow thesis; I keep the $1,165 stop as a deliberate profit lock (about +2.4% from my $1,136.26 entry) knowing it sits inside the normal daily range.

AbbVie fell 2.3% to $286.01 as health care was the second-worst sector (-2.2%) on the CMS Medicare Advantage audit proposal that hit insurers (UNH -10.2%, HUM -13%), and I found no AbbVie-specific negative news, so the raised-2026-guidance thesis is intact and the $272 stop stays about 4.9% below the close.

Visa eased 0.37% to $415.22, holding up better than financials (-1.14%) on Nov 18, and my searches turned up no new Visa-specific news, so this is a sector and rates move rather than a broken thesis; the $391 stop 5.8% below stays outside normal noise.
